title: Shiproom Throttle Sentinel — Standup Notes & Action Log
body:
Date: 2025-02-19
Meeting: Shiproom daily standup (throttle sentinel working group) — notes + action log
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marco, Lena, Sven, Priya (observability), Dan (infra on-call) — partial drop-ins from SRE
Duration: ~35m (standup+tech spike)

Agenda:
- Quick incident recap from last weekend (post-canary spike, throttling cascade)
- Review automated mitigation (Throttle Sentinel) design draft
- Change-log consolidator: plan to avoid noisy rollouts
- Decide short-term release window adjustments and guardrails for next two trains
- Action items, owners, due dates

Incident recap (summary):
- Saturday 02/15, 03:42 UTC: an aggressive canary traffic pattern against model-x-1 triggered continuous batching growth and KV cache churn.
- Observed symptom: per-instance CPU scheduling spike -> grpc queueing -> request timeouts -> automated retry loop from client -> transient overload across the pool.
- Immediate fix: manual scale-out + temporarily reduce canary target from 10% to 2% (hotfix rolled by infra at 04:10 UTC).
- Postmortem pointer: ENGREL-4123 (root-cause + timeline).

Notes:
- Not a model bug, more of a serving routing + autoscaling control loop mismatch under certain sequence length distributions.
- Redis-backed prefix cache had a TTL misalignment leading to slightly higher cache-miss rates when simultaneous canaries ran. Worth a follow-up (ENGINF-2987).

Telemetry highlights (quick):
- P95 latency jumped from baseline 80ms -> 430ms during cascade.
- Token processing rate dropped 18% during the window despite scaling.
- Error budget burn observed on two customer SLAs (ticketed).

Throttle Sentinel (automated mitigation) — design sketch (decisions from meeting):
- Goal: detect early signs of orchestration-induced overload and take minimal, reversible actions before human intervention.
- Inputs to sentinel: moving-window of grpc queue depth, continuous batch size distribution, KV cache miss rate, region-specific CPU scheduling anomalies, canary allocation percentage.
- Rules engine: priority-based policy (fast path) + ML lite anomaly score (slow path). Fast path rules for: queue_depth > 75th percentile AND batch_size > configured threshold -> apply immediate mitigation.
- Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
  1) throttle new canary traffic by shifting target -> from 10% -> to 1-3% (configurable per-train)
  2) reduce batch_max_size on affected pool (temporary override)
  3) flip routing to warm-variant model (model-x-1-quantized) if available
  4) schedule ephemeral scale-up but with cooldown to avoid runaway autoscaling
- Reversion policy: automatic revert after 10m stable signals OR keep until human approves via shiproom page.
- Safety: sentinel MUST NOT evict customer-reserved capacity (Dedicated pools). Only applies to shared/hosted pools.
- Telemetry hooks: emit sentinel decisions to observability with trace id, decision reason, pre/post metrics.

Implementation plan (MVP):
- Phase 1 (spike) — 1 week: prototype rule engine as a k8s cronjob with synthetic inputs. Owner: Marco. Deliverable: working prototype + test harness.
- Phase 2 (pilot) — 2 weeks: integrate with circuit-breaker api and release behind feature flag. Owner: Lena. Deliverable: feature-flagged sentinel in staging + test canaries.
- Phase 3 (rollout) — 1 week: opt-in for next release train, monitored ramp. Owner: Sven. Deliverable: documented runbook and auto-revert dashboards.

Change-log consolidator (new utility):
- Problem: every micro-change creates noisy release notes and inconsistent change windows; shiproom manual merges lead to human error.
- Proposal: single consolidator job that consumes PR labels (release/train/impact), aggregates changelog entries, dedups similar bullet points, and emits a human-editable markdown snippet for the shiproom.
- Integration: will hook into release-ci pipeline and produce an artifact linked to the train. Accepts overrides by release manager.
- Quick spec: python script + small lambda to post to confluence/shiproom. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/521 (work-in-progress). Owner: Priya + release-manager.

Release window guardrails (decisions):
- For next two trains (Feb & Mar): hard cap canary at 5% for canaries involving model architecture changes or new runtime kernels.
- If sentinel fires during train: immediate hold of rollout and escalation to shiproom lead (Aisha).
- Add a preflight checklist item in the release pipeline: verify KV cache TTL parity across pool replicas. Failure -> block.

Action items (concrete):
- Marco: prototype throttle-sentinel rule engine (Phase 1). Due: 2025-02-26. (ENGREL-4123 linked).
- Lena: add feature-flag hooks and test harness in staging; coordinate with QA for synthetic overload runs. Due: 2025-03-05.
- Sven: owner for rollout plan and runbook; create dashboard panels (reversion + decision traces). Due: 2025-03-07.
- Priya: finish change-log consolidator skeleton and open PR; ensure release-ci integration. Due: 2025-02-24.
- Dan (infra on-call): verify autoscaler cooldown config and patch known oscillation for hosted pools; push hotfix to infra-config if safe. Due: 2025-02-22.
- Aisha: update shiproom playbook with new sentinel escalation path and share updated playbook with PMs and SRE. Due: 2025-02-21.

Blockers and open questions:
- Need a clear SLA for automatic reversion time window. 10m proposed but open for discussion. Risks if too short (oscillation) vs too long (customer impact).
- How to test sentinel without creating harmful load on production? Synthetic traffic in a mirrored cluster? (cost concern).
- Should sentinel be allowed to alter per-customer rate limits or only global canary percentages? (privacy/ownership concern).
- Who signs off on 'flip to quantized variant' fallback? Product owners? Legal? (need quick approval path).

Parking lot (future):
- Explore ML-based predictor to forecast cache-churn risk from sequence-length distributions.
- Cross-team tabletop exercise for sentinel-triggered rollbacks — SRE + Product + Sales to rehearse messaging/responses.
- Long-term: bake sentinel decisions into the release orchestration UI (Console) so release managers can preview likely mitigations pre-rollout.

Notes to self / meeting artifacts to attach:
- Attach ENGREL-4123 timeline and raw logs (S3).
- Follow-up: validate Redis TTL alignment across regions (Lena mentioned region replication delay).
- Quick script idea: small canary generator that replays a known traffic trace (from incident) into staging to validate sentinel decisions.

Decisions made in this meeting (explicit):
- Build a lightweight throttle sentinel (rule-first, phased rollout).
- Consolidate change logs via an automated job to reduce noisy roll notes.
- Temporarily reduce canary caps for high-impact trains until sentinel pilot proves stable.

Next meeting: 2025-02-21 shiproom sync. Agenda: Marco demo of phase-1 prototype, Priya update on changelog PR, Dan infra cooldown patch status.

-- end of notes --
